svg.title: 17 GEA run execution
svg.text: GEA run execution · who computes, who decides, who carries
PostgreSQL and API implemented · the Snowflake pipeline is draft SQL that was never executed · the relay is not built.
USER · Vue client → GEA API (Python: validates and records, never computes)
A run is submitted on its own or in a job
A run on its own: at the next claim
A job: in order, MaxParallel at a time
The copy of the status the API reads
JobSummary: status and progress of a job
An execution that went silent is failed,
View RunCancelRequest: cancels to pass on
RELAY · Python, role gea_relay · NOT BUILT
SNOWFLAKE · executes · draft SQL, never executed
The frozen document, same id and SHA-256
Every step reads its configuration from it
One graph run per contract · runs overlap
Each task calls RUN_STEP, which calls the step's procedure GEA.STEP.<STEP>:
set-based SQL, or Snowpark Python where SQL cannot express it
Written before and after every step
RUN_STATUS.CANCEL_REQUESTED_AT: stop before the next step
HOW RUNS ARE ORDERED · decided at submit, enforced in PostgreSQL
in the order of runIds, n at a time
State is rows, written by the system that does the work and copied to the one the user talks to. Nothing in Python computes, waits for, or sequences a step.
A cancelled run is a failed run with the reason. A failed run does not stop its job. To confirm on a real account: several graph runs of one task graph at the same time.
